why: Every side is adjacent to two others, so congruent adjacent pairs force all four sides equal, which is a rhombus.
solution: In quadrilateral \(ABCD\) the adjacent pairs are \(AB, BC\); \(BC, CD\); \(CD, DA\) and \(DA, AB\). If every one of these pairs is congruent, then \(AB = BC\), \(BC = CD\) and \(CD = DA\), so \(AB = BC = CD = DA\). A quadrilateral with all four sides congruent is a rhombus. The other alternatives fail because a rectangle and a parallelogram only need opposite sides congruent, and a trapezium needs only one pair of parallel sides. Hence it is called a rhombus.

why: A square of side a has diagonal a√2, so a√2 = 12√2 gives a = 12 and perimeter 4a = 48 cm.
solution: Let the side of the square be \(a\) cm. A square has a right angle between adjacent sides, so by Pythagoras' theorem the diagonal is \(\sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2}\). Given \(a\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2}\), so \(a = 12\) cm. Perimeter \(= 4a = 4 \times 12 = 48\) cm.

why: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its opposite angles are congruent: 2x = 3x − 40 gives x = 40.
solution: A rhombus is a parallelogram, and the opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent. So \(2x = 3x - 40\), which gives \(3x - 2x = 40\), that is \(x = 40\). (Check: both opposite angles then measure \(80^{\circ}\), and the other pair measures \(100^{\circ}\) each, so the four angles total \(360^{\circ}\).) Hence \(x = 40\).
